result:
12 rules in `pricebook.py` didn't match their docstrings. I fixed all 12 so the code now follows the docstrings, including the module docstring's general rules.

| Rule | Was | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 02, 149 (whole) | Rounded the discount with `round()` | Rounds down to the won (`// 100`) |
| 15, 38, 89 (marginal) | Rounded the discount with `round()` | Rounds down to the won (`// 100`) |
| 32 | `qty > 5`, so exactly 5 units got no discount | `qty >= 5` |
| 74 | `qty >= 31`, so exactly 30 units got no discount | `qty >= 30` |
| 60 | Capped the price at 30,000 won, then took 10% of it | Takes 10% of the full price, then caps the discount at 30,000 won |
| 119 | 16% off | 15% off |
| 126 | 11% off | 10% off |
| 121 | Only capped the discount when it was over 60,000 won, so discounts between 30,000 and 60,000 won weren't capped | Always caps the discount at 30,000 won |
| 140 | Discounted only the units above 20 (marginal) | Discounts all units (whole), as its docstring says |

**How I checked it:** I wrote a separate script that reads each rule's type, percentage, threshold and cap from its docstring and works out the expected amount. It compared every rule against the actual code over about 2,000 combinations of quantity and unit price, including the exact thresholds and values that land on the cap.
- **Before the fix:** exactly these 12 rules were wrong.
- **After the fix:** no rule differs, and every result is a whole number.
- **Negative inputs:** I also confirmed that every rule raises `ValueError` for a negative quantity or price.

The changes are limited to these 12 discount calculations and conditions. I didn't touch any other code or any docstring.

STATUS: DONE
